item.title: Asia Stocks Rise, Bonds Steady Before US Inflation: Markets Wrap
item.author: Bloomberg News (English)
item.description: Bonds remained in focus after yields on the longest-maturity Treasuries reached their highest since 2002 in the New York session. Yields steadied across the curve after rising earlier this week, as a rally in oil prompted traders to price in further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. Brent climbed 0.5% to about $103.10 a barrel, recouping some of the losses from Tuesday.

item.title: Funds Buy Australian Bonds on Signal Rate Hikes Are Nearing End
item.author: Bloomberg News (English)
item.description: Investors are starting to snap up Australian bonds, betting that the Reserve Bank is nearing the end of its rate-hike cycle after lifting borrowing costs to a 15-year high. Schroders Plc bought three-year bonds on Tuesday, while Franklin Templeton said it prefers securities maturing in two to three years. RBA Governor Michele Bullock expressed “hope” that the four hikes this year are sufficient to bring inflation back to target.

item.title: Weitere Kosten drohen
item.author: Finanz und Wirtschaft
item.description: Die Kosten für den Kauf und Verkauf von Titeln springen zuerst ins Auge. Wer jedoch nur auf Courtagen achtet, übersieht leicht die Nebenkosten abseits des Handels. Depotgebühren, Währungsaufschläge und Spesen für Steuerdokumente schmälern die Rendite zusätzlich. Vor dem Depotabschluss sollten Anleger die laufenden Haltekosten von Aktien prüfen. Neon, Yuh und Saxo verzichten komplett auf Depotgebühren.
